Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 73, verses 1–4:

Naming of the surah

• It is called al-Muzzammil (the one wrapped up), because it opens with the Prophet's address (ﷺ) using this description, meaning: the one covered with a garment or the like.

From the aims of the surah

• An indication of the weight of the revelation that Allah entrusted to His Messenger (ﷺ), and His command to seek help in bearing it by spending the night in worship, and His affirmation of him in this; and His command to turn away from the denial of the polytheists and to be patient over their harm.

• An admonition to the polytheists with what befell the people of Pharaoh when they denied the Messenger of Allah sent to them, and a warning to them of punishment, retribution and terror on the Day of Resurrection.

• Praise of a group of believers who were constant in standing in prayer at night, a command to persist in establishing the prayer, paying the zakah and giving charity, and a promise of great reward for good deeds.

[Tafsir]

"O you who are wrapped up in your garment, stand [in prayer] during the night, except for a little of it: stand for half the night, or reduce it slightly from half, until you reach a third, or add to the half until you reach two-thirds, and recite the Qur'an slowly and deliberately, clearly articulating the letters and the pauses."

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 73, verse 6:**

Worship that arises in the depths of the night has a stronger effect on the heart and is more articulate in speech, because the heart is free from the preoccupations of this world.
Indeed, during the day you have considerable movement and occupation with your affairs and with the matters of the message, so devote yourself at night to the worship of your Lord.

And remember, O Prophet, the name of your Lord, and call upon Him by it, and devote yourself to Him wholeheartedly in your worship, and put your trust in Him. He is the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, so rely upon Him and entrust your affairs to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 73, verse 10:

Be patient over what the polytheists say about you and about your religion, oppose them in their false actions, while turning away from them and leaving off avenging yourself upon them.

Leave Me alone with those who deny, the people of luxury and comfort in this world, O Messenger, and give them respite for a little while, by delaying the punishment from them until their term (of the Book) reaches its appointed end with their punishment.

Indeed, for them with Us in the Hereafter are heavy shackles and a blazing fire in which they will be burned, and food that is repulsive, sticking in the throat and impossible to swallow, and a painful torment.

On the day when the earth and the mountains will be shaken and convulsed, until the mountains become a heap of sand, flowing and scattered, after they had been solid and firm.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 73, verses 15–16:

Indeed, We have sent to you, O people of Makkah, Muhammad as a messenger, a witness against you for what has proceeded from you of disbelief and disobedience, just as We sent Musa (Moses) as a messenger to the tyrant Pharaoh. But Pharaoh denied Musa, did not believe in his message, and disobeyed his command, so We seized him with a severe seizing. In the verse there is a warning against disobeying the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), lest the disobedient one suffer the same as what befell Pharaoh and his people.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 73, verses 15–16:

Indeed, We have sent to you, O people of Makkah, Muhammad as a messenger, a witness against you for what has proceeded from you of disbelief and disobedience, just as We sent Musa (Moses) as a messenger to the tyrant Pharaoh. But Pharaoh denied Musa, did not believe in his message, and disobeyed his command, so We seized him with a severe seizing. In the verse there is a warning against disobeying the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), lest the disobedient one suffer the same as what befell Pharaoh and his people.
How will you protect yourselves, if you disbelieve, from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, the Day that will turn the young children gray-haired because of its intense terror and distress?
The heaven will be split apart on that Day, because of its terrible severity. The promise of Allah, the Exalted, concerning the coming of that Day was bound to take place without any doubt.

These frightening verses, which contain the crashing blows and the warnings, are an admonition and a lesson for mankind. Whoever wishes to take heed and benefit from them should take obedience and piety as a path that leads him to the good pleasure of his Lord, who created him and nurtured him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 73, verse 20:

Indeed your Lord, O Prophet, knows that you stand in worship at night (tahajjud) for less than two-thirds of it at times, stand for half of it at times, and stand for a third of it at other times, and a group of your companions stand with you. And Allah alone is the One who determines the night and the day, and knows their measures and what passes and what remains of them. Allah knew that you would not be able to stand the whole night, so He lightened it for you. So recite in prayer at night whatever portion of the Qur'an is easy for you to recite. Allah knew that among you there would be those whom illness prevents from standing in the night, and there would be other people who travel through the earth for trade and work, seeking from the provision of Allah that which is lawful, and other people who strive in the way of Allah to raise His word and spread His religion. So recite in your prayer whatever portion of the Qur'an is easy for you, persevere in the obligatory prayers, give the obligatory zakat, and give charity in the ways of righteousness and kindness from your wealth, seeking the Face of Allah. Whatever good you do in the ways of righteousness, goodness and acts of obedience, you will find its reward with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, better than what you sent forth in this world, and greater in reward. And seek the forgiveness of Allah in all your circumstances. Indeed Allah is Forgiving toward you and Merciful to you.
